clue.text: One takes in American show

parts.note: ER is the long-running American hospital drama on television

explanation.surface: Someone attends a performance in the States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One takes in' looks like the start of a sentence about seeing a show; it is the definition, a person who cons or exploits others.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who exploits others takes them in, and drug takers are also called this.

clue.text: Amplifies first half of number, stage rocks

indicators.note: rocks as a verb means shakes or unsettles, so these letters are jumbled
the opening three of the six letters of number are kept

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A band turns up the volume as the opening of a song shakes the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rocks' shuffles NUM (the first half of 'number') with STAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean increases or makes larger, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Fusses over big promotion

indicators.note: in a down answer, over means the first piece is placed above the second

parts.note: an ad is a promotion or advertisement
OS stands for outsize, meaning big

explanation.surface: People complain about a major marketing push.
explanation.definitionFit: An ado is a fuss or commotion, as in much ado about nothing; plural for plural.

clue.text: One agrees American's behind record

parts.note: ass is the American word for the backside
to enter is to record, as in a ledger

explanation.surface: Someone goes along with things, being an American following a disc.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who gives assent is someone who consents or concurs.

clue.text: Partner to want me?

parts.note: to miss is to want or long for someone absent
in British colloquial speech us means me, as in give us a kiss

explanation.surface: Someone asks their partner whether they long for them.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal British term for one's wife, the other half of a couple.

clue.text: Those planning school education changing rules

indicators.note: changing tells us these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Planners in education alter the rules of a school.
explanation.definitionFit: People who draw up timetables are planners; both nouns name organisers of time.

clue.text: Relating to an element from piece Rick picked up

indicators.note: picked up means heard, so the words are said out loud

parts.note: a knight is a chess piece; taken as a name, spoken as written

explanation.surface: A chemistry fact comes from a bit of something a man called Rick overheard.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken, 'knight Rick' sounds just like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes compounds of nitrogen, a chemical element.

clue.text: Emerging from backstage: Supertramp Forever

indicators.note: Emerging from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A rock band takes an eternity to come out from behind the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, a very long time feels like for ever, as in waiting all this time.

clue.text: Recording of Logical Song

parts.note: sound reasoning is logical reasoning
a track is a song on an album

explanation.surface: A recording of the Supertramp hit The Logical Song.
explanation.walkthrough: The Logical Song is a 1979 Supertramp single, part of the puzzle's theme.
explanation.definitionFit: The music accompanying a film is its audio recording, sold as an album.

clue.text: Taking long way home — good theatrical closure?

indicators.note: Taking means the first piece takes on the next one straight after it

parts.note: ST is short for street, a way
to itch for something is to long for it
someone who is in is at home

explanation.surface: Supertramp's Take the Long Way Home brings a show to a satisfying end.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the Long Way Home is a Supertramp song. The theatre here is an operating theatre, where a wound is closed with sutures.
explanation.definitionFit: Surgeons close an incision with sutures, sewing it shut after an operation.

clue.text: Makes new recording with band, while mixing rest

parts.note: REM is an American rock band
as can mean while, as in as I was leaving

indicators.note: mixing, a studio term, tells us these letters are blended into a new order

explanation.surface: A band goes back to the studio to remix the remaining tracks.
explanation.definitionFit: Producing a fresh master copy of old audio improves its sound quality.

clue.text: Makes number listeners must take in

indicators.note: take in means the listeners hold the other piece inside them

parts.note: ears are what we listen with

explanation.surface: A singer produces a song that the audience has to absorb.
explanation.definitionFit: To make money is to be paid it, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Precise playing parts later

indicators.note: parts means splits open, so the other piece goes into the middle

parts.note: a tight performance is precise
a play or record that is on is playing

explanation.surface: A band delivers an exact performance of its sections afterwards.
explanation.definitionFit: This evening is later in the day, the sense of an adverb of time.

clue.text: See 9
Sugar's stirred with it twice for musicians

indicators.note: stirred, as with sugar in tea, tells us these letters are mixed up
twice means the little word it is taken two times

explanation.surface: Something sweet is mixed in a couple of times for the band.
explanation.definitionFit: Players of a six-stringed instrument are a kind of musician.

clue.text: Well excited — do Give a Little Bit

parts.note: so can stand for well, as in so, what now?
up means excited or keyed up
to do someone is to con or cheat them

explanation.surface: An eager fan rushes to play Supertramp's song Give a Little Bit.
explanation.walkthrough: Give a Little Bit is a 1977 Supertramp single; 'Give' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: A French borrowing for a tiny amount or trace, such as of garlic.

clue.text: Very much turned on before climax

indicators.note: turned means the little word on is reversed

parts.note: the end of something is its climax

explanation.surface: Someone is greatly aroused as things approach a peak.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means hugely or a great deal, as in it pleased me immensely.

clue.text: As discussed, mostly very musical

indicators.note: mostly means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: something discussed has been said

explanation.surface: As already agreed, the piece is extremely tuneful.
explanation.definitionFit: In musical directions the Italian term means extremely, as in allegro assai.

clue.text: Bloody right? Not politically

definitions.meaning: in politics the colour stands for the left wing, socialists, not the right

explanation.surface: Someone says something indignant, then denies any political meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: The colour of blood, and the traditional colour of socialism, the political left.

clue.text: Decline drink before performance

parts.note: to down a drink is to swallow it in one
a turn is an act or performance, as at a variety show

explanation.surface: Someone refuses a drink before going on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A fall in economic activity is a slump or decline.

clue.text: Announce Tramp to return with start of Crime?

indicators.note: to return means the pronoun is turned backwards

parts.note: the setter Tramp refers to himself, so the word stands for me
the start of Crime is the letter C, written out as its spelt name

explanation.surface: The setter declares a return with the beginning of a detective story.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that C is spelt out as its name, CEE.
explanation.definitionFit: To act as master of ceremonies is to host and introduce the acts.

clue.text: Perhaps, Breakfast in America's Goodbye Stranger at the start

parts.note: cheerio is an informal British goodbye

indicators.note: at the start means only the opening letter of Stranger is used

explanation.surface: Two Supertramp titles, Breakfast in America and Goodbye Stranger, are run together.
explanation.walkthrough: Breakfast in America is a 1979 Supertramp album and Goodbye Stranger a single from it.
explanation.definitionFit: A popular US oat cereal brand is an example of a morning meal in the States.

clue.text: Two stupid people contracted wise guy?

indicators.note: contracted means each of the two words is shortened by its last letter

parts.note: knob and wally are both British slang for a fool

explanation.surface: A pair of idiots are hired by a smart alec.
explanation.definitionFit: A smart alec who thinks they have every fact is a wise guy, ironically.

clue.text: Comes clean with personal statement, primarily in court

parts.note: your own is personal to you

indicators.note: primarily means just the first letter of statement

parts.note: to be up before the magistrate is to be in court

explanation.surface: A defendant confesses in a personal statement given at trial.
explanation.definitionFit: To admit something is to confess, the idiom for coming clean.

clue.text: Look at coloured light on gallery

parts.note: lo is an old word for look, as in lo and behold
UV is ultraviolet light, lying beyond the violet colour
re means on or concerning

explanation.surface: Visitors admire stained-glass light shining on an art gallery.
explanation.definitionFit: The Paris museum housing the Mona Lisa is a famous art gallery.

clue.text: London stages finale with set arranged first

indicators.note: first means this group comes before the other piece
arranged means these letters are put in a different order

parts.note: the finale is the end

explanation.surface: A theatre production ends with its scenery put in place first.
explanation.walkthrough: The West End is London's commercial theatre district.
explanation.definitionFit: London's theatreland, so the name stands for its many stages.

clue.text: Muslims surrounded by students revolting

indicators.note: revolting means turning over, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: something surrounded by others is in them
NUS is the National Union of Students

explanation.surface: Muslims find themselves surrounded by protesting students.
explanation.definitionFit: The larger of the two main branches of Islam, its followers.

clue.text: Show clue for Supertramp?

parts.note: the band's name splits into super, read as ..., and tramp, read as ..., so the title would clue it

explanation.surface: Asking which TV programme might be a clue for the band Supertramp.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-running American science-fiction television series.

clue.text: Turned out bad, didn't do School?

indicators.note: bad signals the letters go wrong and are reordered

explanation.surface: Someone turned out badly because they skipped school.
explanation.walkthrough: School is a Supertramp song, part of the theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone without formal teaching never received schooling.

clue.text: See 26
Enough time for song

parts.note: due means adequate or enough, as in with due care

explanation.surface: Sufficient time is allowed for a song.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece sung by two performers is a type of song.

clue.text: Man with another man's woman is kinky later (and rude)

indicators.note: kinky means twisted, so the letters are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: An affair with someone's wife is called perverse and offensive.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sleeping with a person other than their spouse commits infidelity.

clue.text: Run off with band to record backing

parts.note: ELO is the Electric Light Orchestra, a rock band

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the letters are reversed

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: A musician leaves with a group to make a backing track.
explanation.definitionFit: Couples who run away secretly to marry are said to do this.
